must_identify.item: The worker container is OOMKilled (terminated reason OOMKilled), not crashing for another reason
must_identify.evidence: This mismatch between live config and tracked config, combined with the OOMKilled/Exit Code 137 termination reason observed on the pod [6], confirms the kernel OOM killer terminated the container due to the oversized in-memory batch allocation — not an application-level crash or cluster-wide resource shortage

must_identify.item: The trigger is the BATCH_SIZE change from 500 to 2500 (or the larger batch exceeding the limit)
must_identify.evidence: The worker code allocates `BATCH_SIZE × 100KiB` of memory per cycle [10], so at BATCH_SIZE=2500 this amounts to roughly 244MiB, exceeding the container's 192Mi memory limit confirmed via pod describe [6]; at the originally intended BATCH_SIZE=500 this would be ~49MiB, safely under the limit.

notes: The RCA correctly identifies the OOMKill and the BATCH_SIZE 500→2500 trigger, and it explicitly rules out node pressure. It gives no explicit remediation, only noting that 500 would fit under the limit, so the fix could not be graded.
